name: Yashwanth Muppidi
headline: Building machines that move through the real world.
intro: Mechanical engineer working across humanoid robotics, product development, mechatronics, and autonomous systems.
about: I am a mechanical engineering student at Purdue University, focused on the hardware that lets robotic and autonomous systems operate outside the lab.

My work spans mechanism design, prototyping, test hardware, fabrication, and system integration. I am most interested in the point where careful mechanical decisions become reliable physical behavior.

principles.title: Design for the system
principles.text: Mechanical decisions are made with controls, electronics, assembly, and field use in view.

principles.title: Build to learn
principles.text: Prototypes, fixtures, and tests turn assumptions into evidence early.

principles.title: Make it legible
principles.text: Clear interfaces, drawings, and documentation are part of the engineering work.

experience.summary: Designed and tested hardware for autonomous aircraft operations, spanning deployment equipment, test fixtures, and reliability work.
Supported surgical robotics and medical-device development through end-effector prototyping, embedded controls, assembly fixtures, and testing.
Leading mechanical development for NEMO, a bipedal humanoid robotics platform.
